headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Cline can write/egress broadly while semantica shares a context graph and handles secrets, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and uses MCP; semantica ingests local files, MCP resources, and shares a context graph across agents. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if one agent writes attacker-controlled content that the other later parses. The pathway is documented by both profiles, though not directly observed.
conditions: IF Cline writes untrusted text into shared workspace files or MCP resources
IF semantica later treats those files or MCP resources as instructions or provenance
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP sharing between the pair
Add content provenance tags before parsing
Require manual review of cross-agent file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline has broad filesystem and browser access and handles model-provider API keys; semantica touches enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and secrets such as private keys. Because both read/write files and semantica also consumes many external data sources, a shared workspace can expose sensitive material across the pair. The blast radius includes secrets and regulated data.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same filesystem workspace
IF either agent stores secrets or regulated documents in that workspace
mitigations: Use separate OS users or containers
Mount only read-only inputs to one agent
Move secrets to a dedicated vault path
Block browser downloads into shared folders
Run a quick audit for shared workspace paths

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use MCP. Cline’s session is workspace-scoped via filesystem, while semantica uses a shared intelligence layer across agents. Without explicit locking, concurrent writes to the same repo or graph can corrupt state or overwrite each other’s changes.
conditions: IF both agents target the same git repository or directory
IF no external lock or transaction layer serializes writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Enable file or repo locking
Serialize git commits through one agent
Pause one agent during package installs
Use a staging branch per agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate browser-derived outputs and file edits, and semantica’s deterministic graph/provenance layer can ingest those outputs as structured facts. If semantica treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream decision records, audit trails, or actions. The pair’s documented file and MCP pathways make this a default-risk interaction.
conditions: IF semantica ingests Cline-produced files or MCP outputs without verification
IF downstream workflows persist those outputs into decision records or audit trails
mitigations: Require source verification before ingestion
Insert a human approval step for cross-agent facts
Mark Cline outputs as untrusted by default
Log provenance on every handoff
Limit semantica to read-only consumption of Cline artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles browser screenshots and model-provider keys, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and private keys. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because semantica’s data classes are broader and more sensitive, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated enterprise data is routed through Cline’s browser or workspace
IF semantica’s deployment lacks matching retention or residency controls
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Keep regulated data out of browser screenshots
Document retention settings for both agents
Restrict semantica to non-regulated datasets
Review vendor residency and DPA terms
